title: Surjectivity of a finite type ring map descends along a directed colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $A_i\to A_{i'}$ for $i\le i'$, compatible), with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $0\in I$, let $B_0$ and $C_0$ be commutative $A_0$-algebras and $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras which is of finite type ($C_0$ is generated as a $B_0$-algebra, via $\varphi_0$, by finitely many elements). For $i\ge0$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-algebra via the transition map, and $A$ via the coprojection, and put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi_i=\mathrm{id}_{A_i}\otimes\varphi_0:B_i\to C_i$, and $B=A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\varphi_0:B\to C$. If $\varphi$ is surjective, then there is an $i\ge0$ such that $\varphi_i$ is surjective (Stacks Algebra, Lemma 07RH).

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RH (lemma-colimit-surjective, line 47547; tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags line 9867) and its proof (generators $x_1,\dots,x_m$ of $C_0$ over $B_0$, preimages $b_j\in A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$ of $1\otimes x_j$, lifted to a finite stage, where they map to $1\otimes x_j$ after increasing $i$)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the rings and maps, and their compatibilities).* Write $\alpha_{i'i}:A_i\to A_{i'}$ ($i\le i'$) for the transition maps and $\alpha_i:A_i\to A$ for the coprojections, so $\alpha_{i'}\circ\alpha_{i'i}=\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_{i''i'}\circ\alpha_{i'i}=\alpha_{i''i}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $T$ equal to $A_i$ ($i\ge0$) or to $A$, the $A_0$-modules $B_T=T\otimes_{A_0}B_0$ and $C_T=T\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ [def-weil-module-base-change] are commutative rings with $(t\otimes b)(t'\otimes b')=tt'\otimes bb'$ and unit $1\otimes1$, additively spanned by the pure tensors. For $0\le i\le i'$ put $\mu^B_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'i}\otimes\mathrm{id}:B_i\to B_{i'}$, $\mu^B_i=\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id}:B_i\to B$, and likewise $\mu^C_{i'i}$, $\mu^C_i$ with $C_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-map-ring-hom] (applied to the $A_0$-algebra maps $\alpha_{i'i}$, $\alpha_i$ with $N=B_0$ or $C_0$, and to $\varphi_0$ with $N=T$, composed with the symmetry isomorphisms $T\otimes_{A_0}N\cong N\otimes_{A_0}T$, which are ring isomorphisms) the maps $\mu^B_{i'i},\mu^B_i,\mu^C_{i'i},\mu^C_i$ and $\varphi_i,\varphi$ are ring homomorphisms. Moreover (a) $\varphi_{i'}\circ\mu^B_{i'i}=\mu^C_{i'i}\circ\varphi_i$ and (b) $\varphi\circ\mu^B_i=\mu^C_i\circ\varphi_i$, since both sides of (a) send $a\otimes b\mapsto\alpha_{i'i}(a)\otimes\varphi_0(b)$, both sides of (b) send $a\otimes b\mapsto\alpha_i(a)\otimes\varphi_0(b)$, and all maps are additive; (c) $\mu^B_{i'}\circ\mu^B_{i'i}=\mu^B_i$, $\mu^B_{i''i'}\circ\mu^B_{i'i}=\mu^B_{i''i}$ and the same for $C$, by the relations among the $\alpha$'s, checked on pure tensors; (d) $\mu^C_{i'i}(1\otimes c)=1\otimes c$ and $\mu^C_i(1\otimes c)=1\otimes c$ for $c\in C_0$, the $\alpha$'s being unital.

proof.text: *Step 2 (generators and their preimages over $A$).* As $\varphi_0$ is of finite type, choose $x_1,\dots,x_m\in C_0$ generating $C_0$ as a $B_0$-algebra via $\varphi_0$, i.e. every element of $C_0$ is a finite sum of terms $\varphi_0(b)x_1^{\nu_1}\cdots x_m^{\nu_m}$ with $b\in B_0$. Since $\varphi$ is surjective, choose $b_j\in B$ with $\varphi(b_j)=1\otimes x_j$ in $C$, $j=1,\dots,m$. (Stacks: 'Let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ be generators for $C_0$ over $B_0$. Pick $b_j\in A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$ mapping to $1\otimes x_j$'.)

*Step 3 (lifting the $b_j$ to a stage).* By [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise](1) with $M_0=B_0$ (so $M_i=B_i$, $M=B$, $\mu_i=\mu^B_i$), each $b_j$ equals $\mu^B_{i_j}(t_j)$ for some $i_j\ge0$ and $t_j\in B_{i_j}$. $I$ being directed, choose $i\in I$ with $i\ge0$ and $i\ge i_j$ for all $j$ (any $i\ge0$ if $m=0$), and replace $t_j$ by $\mu^B_{ii_j}(t_j)\in B_i$; by step 1(c), $\mu^B_i(t_j)=b_j$ for all $j$. (Stacks: 'For some $i\ge0$ we can find $b_{j,i}\in A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0$ mapping to $b_j$'.)

*Step 4 (the lifts hit $1\otimes x_j$ after increasing $i$).* Put $d_j=\varphi_i(t_j)-1\otimes x_j\in C_i$. By step 1(b),(d), $\mu^C_i(d_j)=\varphi(\mu^B_i(t_j))-1\otimes x_j=\varphi(b_j)-1\otimes x_j=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise](2) with $M_0=C_0$ (so $\mu_i=\mu^C_i$, $\mu_{i'i}=\mu^C_{i'i}$) there is $i'_j\ge i$ with $\mu^C_{i'_ji}(d_j)=0$. Choose $i'\ge i'_j$ for all $j$ ($i'=i$ if $m=0$); by step 1(c), $\mu^C_{i'i}(d_j)=\mu^C_{i'i'_j}(\mu^C_{i'_ji}(d_j))=0$. Put $t'_j=\mu^B_{i'i}(t_j)\in B_{i'}$. By step 1(a),(d), $\varphi_{i'}(t'_j)=\mu^C_{i'i}(\varphi_i(t_j))=\mu^C_{i'i}(1\otimes x_j)+\mu^C_{i'i}(d_j)=1\otimes x_j$ in $C_{i'}$ for all $j$. (Stacks: 'After increasing $i$ we may assume that $b_{j,i}$ maps to $1\otimes x_j$ in $A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ for all $j$'.)
